"This database contains receipts, spending and fiscal aggregates back to 1700. These are not national statistics and judgements have been made in places to ensure consistency in the figures across years. A full list of notes and sources is provided at the bottom. 


Choose a chart from the dropdown menu:"
"All data, unless otherwise stated, are on a March-ending financial year basis. For non March-ending financial years, figures are linearly interpolated. "
"Unless otherwise stated, figures are from the Bank of England millennium dataset until 1948-49 and ONS thereafter. ONS figures are consistent with the 23 May Public Sector Finances release. "
"Receipts are on a cash basis until 1998-99 and accruals basis thereafter. "

"1Income tax, NICs, Capital Gains Tax and Windfall tax receipts sourced from Bank of England millennium dataset until 1998-99. National insurance contributions are consistent with social security contributions from Middleton (1996) until 1946-47. "
"2Corporation tax series is consistent with ONS series N445 prior to 1999-00 and CPRN thereafter. "

"3Petroleum revenue tax, petroleum royalties, gas levy are consistent with table 11.11 from ONS 'Statistics of government revenues from UK oil and gas production' (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/government-revenues-from-uk-oil-and-gas-production--2)"
"4VAT receipts are inclusive of refunds to central and local government bodies. "
"5Prior to 1999-00, custom and excise duties are consistent with ONS series NMYB less GTBC"
"6Other central government receipts includes smaller receipts lines, as well as central government interest and dividends and gross operating surplus. "
"7An adjustment has been made to central government receipts in 1919-20 and 1920-21 to ensure consistency with total public sector receipts. "
"8Other public sector receipts includes smaller non-central government receipts, as well as non-central government interest and dividends and gross operating surplus. "
"A number of sources are used to compile the various spending component time series"

"1Central Government uses Mitchell (1988)  from 1700-01 to 1899-00, and then the Bank of England millennium dataset from 1994-95, then ONS data for 1995-96 to 2020-21 and OBR data in 2021-22 and 2022-23. "
"2Total Public Sector uses the Bank of England from 1900-01 to 1954-55, then IFS data from 1955-56 to 2019-20 and then OBR data from 2020-21 to 2022-23."
"3Current Spending is a residual derived by subtracting columns D and E."

"4Public Sector Gross Investment used the Bank of England millennium dataset from 1856-57 to 1954-55,  then IFS data from 1955-56 to 2019-20 and then OBR data from 2020-21 to 2022-23. N.B. There is a gap in the data between 1939-40 and 1945-46."

"5Defence uses Mitchell (1988)  from 1700-01 to 1854-55, then the Bank of England millennium dataset from 1855-56 to 1954-55, then IFS data from 1955-56 to 2019-20, then Public Expenditure Statistics Analyses (PESA) data for 2020-21 to 2021-22, and then 2022-23 is grown using growth rate between 2020-21 and 2021-22."

"6Health uses the Bank of England millennium dataset from 1920-21 to 1954-55, then IFS data from 1955-56 to 2019-20, then PESA data for 2020-21 to 2021-22, and then 2022-23 is grown using growth rate between 2020-21 and 2021-22. N.B There are datagaps between 1939-40 to 1947-48 due to insufficient data availability"
"7Social Security uses IFS data from 1955-56 to 2021-22, then 2022-23 is grown using the growth rate between 2020-21 and 2021-22."
"o/w pensioners uses IFS data from 1978-79 to 2021-22, then 2022-23 is the same proportion of overall Social Security spending as 2021-22."
"o/w non-pensioners uses IFS data from 1978-79 to 2021-22, then 2022-23 is the same proportion of overall Social Security spending as 2021-22."

"8Education uses the Bank of England millennium dataset from 1920-21 to 1954-55, then IFS data from 1955-56 to 2019-20, and PESA data for 2020-21 to 2021-22 and then is grown using growth rate between 2020-21 and 2021-22. N.B There are datagaps between 1939-40 to 1947-48 due to insufficient data availability"

"9Debt Interest uses Mitchell (1988)  from 1700-01 to 1854-55, then the Bank of England millennium dataset from 1855-56 to 1947-48, then OBR calculations from ONS data from 1948-49 to 2022-23. Debt interest spending is Central Government net of the APF."
"10Other Public Sector Spending is a residual derived by subtracting columns D-G-H-I-L-M"
"For years 1915-16 to 1919-20, total Public Sector spending is equal to total Central Government spending due differences between data sources."

"1 PSNB sourced from Bank of England (2017) from 1700-01 to 1899-00, then from OBR (2023) for 1900-01 onwards. Due to availability of data, from 1700-01 to 1899-00 our PSNB series is showing Central Government Net Borrowing. "
"2 PSND sourced from Bank of England (2017) from 1700-01 to 1899-00, then from OBR (2023) for 1900-01 onwards. "

"3 Note on coverage of the nominal GDP series which follows the political boundaries in place at any given time:
- From 1700-01 to 1800-01, Great Britain GDP (England, Wales and Scotland) – this is a simplification of the historical political boundaries as the Exchequer only started imposing taxes on Scotland post the commencement of the Acts of Union on 1 May 1707. 
- From 1800-01 to 1921-22, GB and Irish (both North and South) GDP, receipts and spending from the Exchequer covered the whole of the UK and Ireland’s geography at that time. 
- From 1922-23 onwards GB and Northern Irish GDP as Anglo-Irish Treaty came fully into effect on 31 March 1922."
"Bank of England, A Millennium of UK Data , 2017"
"Middleton. R, Government versus the market: the growth of the public sector, economic management and British economic performance, c.1890-1979, 1996"
"Institute for Fiscal Studies, IFS spending composition, June 2021"
"HM Treasury, Public Sector Expenditure Analyses, July 2022"
